Flame in a Fireball – NASA

Introduction

A fireball is a very bright meteor that enters the Earth's atmosphere from outer space. According to NASA, fireballs are brighter than ordinary meteors and can sometimes shine even brighter than the full Moon. They are formed when small space rocks, called meteoroids, travel through Earth's atmosphere at very high speeds.

details:
Flame in Free Fall is a NASA experiment that studies how fire behaves in space under microgravity conditions.

On Earth, flames usually have a teardrop shape because hot air rises due to gravity. But in space, hot air does not rise normally, so flames can become round or spherical.

NASA scientists study these flames to understand how fire burns in space and to improve astronaut safety.

Main Purpose: To understand fire behaviour in microgravity and make spacecraft safer.

Applications:

Space research

Fire safety in spacecraft

Understanding combustion

Future space missions
